title.narrative: Project for the Social and Economic Inclusion of Displaced Persons and host communities in urban areas – Burkina Faso

description.narrative:
The deteriorating security situation in the Sahel region, including frequent attacks from unidentified armed groups (“Groupes Armés Non-Identifiés”/ GANI), has forced nearly 2 million people in Burkina Faso to flee their places of origin (primarily from rural to urban areas, specifically to small and intermediate towns). International experience shows that people affected by conflict remain displaced for an average of two decades in the areas they fled to, it is therefore important to advance durable solutions to socially and economically include displaced families into hosting communities and neighbourhoods, ensuring that participatory processes allow both displaced and local communities to express their needs and benefit from planned interventions and investments, while strengthening the role and capacities of local governments. The massive displacement of populations has significant consequences on receiving (and thus rapidly growing) urban centres, especially in terms of accelerated and informal urban sprawl, strong pressure on existing basic/social services (water, electricity, public facilities, etc.) and on natural resources. Competition for access to these services and resources can lead to conflict between local and displaced populations and weaken social cohesion. In addition, displaced populations have often lost their means of subsistence and little opportunities to generate income in (urban) areas of arrival. Many, due to those economic challenges, are forced to live in informal or unplanned settlements, in inadequate shelter / housing and under precarious living conditions, thus aggravating their situation of vulnerability, particularly for women and girls. With food prices rising due to reduced agricultural productivity caused by the instable security situation, displacement and climate change impacts (irregular rains of the previous years), the risks of food insecurity are high for this and coming years in Burkina Faso. The Ukraine crisis, and increased prizes for imported food, add to the challenges. The project therefore proposes an integrated approach, which allows people in vulnerable situations to have increased protection and stability through the access to housing and tenure rights, but also to foster their opportunities and skills to generate income and become more food self-sufficient by enabling them to grow food for their families on the urban plots of limited size allocated to them, and training them to use innovative methodologies for food production and processing thus generating income through establishing small scale businesses in the food chain.
Project approach: The project advocates for and implements an integrated approach for urban displacement context responding to expressed needs as in recent community consultations, where both IDPs and local communities expressed that livelihood opportunities and income generating activities (IGA) would be a high priority for them, once they have access to housing and basic services, such as water and sanitation. The proposed approach will build upon UN-Habitat’s experiences on adequate housing, urban and territorial planning, the safer cities guidelines as well as tools from the Global Land Tool Network (GLTN).
The project approach is aiming for three outcomes:
Outcome 1: “Capacity of local governments is enhanced” Local authorities will be seen as main enablers for participatory urban planning processes and the socio-economic inclusion of people in vulnerable situations. Urban experts will be deployed to each municipality to support local capacity and multi-stakeholder coordination mechanism will be established (including local authorities from different sectors but also representatives of local and IDP communtiies), where major decision will be discussed on a local and community level. Through trainings and workshops, local authorities will have increased understanding and knowledge on participatory planning processes for developing urban and neighborhood plans (including formalising the newly planned areas) in an inclusive manner. Processes for securing land tenure for beneficiaries will be conducted, led by local actors and including traditional leaders and land owners. The projet aims to help to rebuild trust in government authorities through participatory processes and access to improved living conditions and services but also increased social cohesion between communities, thus fostering development and peace (HDP nexus).
Outcome 2: “Access to decent housing, essential services and facilities are improved” - The project puts “housing at the centre” for a dignified life and enables 300 families (approx. 1800 beneficiaries) to build (incremental) housing units. The idea is to engage communities in planning as well as construtions processes.
